newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Weakness continues.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Weakness continues.

text.p: In traditional late-May fashion, the Gulf oil product market was deathly quiet in the week to Thursday, with traders seeing little light at the end of the tunnel.
They said pressure continued on middle distillate premiums and this was likely to be the case for the next few months.
"The market is weak and oversupplied," said one trader.
"There is very little business," said another.
Gas oil premiums were seen lower than last week's levels.
"It's probably around 15 cents on gas oil. There is nothing really to distinguish the two," said one trader, referring to premiums to spot on 0.5 percent and 1.0 percent gas oil.
Others saw the 1.0 percent grade trading at close to parity to spot and the 0.5 percent gas oil at between parity and a 10-cent premium.

Gulf traders said they were closely watching the Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) gas oil import tender for direction. The results of the tender, seen at 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes, are expected later on Thursday or Friday.
IOC's tender has attracted lower offers on a cost-and-freight basis than the previous two tenders for May and June, which traders said reflected the current soft market.

But on a free-on-board basis, traders said offers were unchanged from the last tender. Kuwait Petroleum Corp offered 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil at a 30-cent premium and the 0.5 percent grade at a 45-cent premium to spot Middle East quotes.
The previous week, traders had put the premiums at 20-30 cents and 35-45 cents respectively.
Gas oil was independently assessed at $23 a barrel fob Gulf from around $23.45 last week.
The premium on jet was seen steady at last week's levels of between five and 20 cents. "If there was any trade, I guess it would be at somewhere between five and 20 plus," said a trader.
Jet was independently assessed at around $22.50 a barrel fob Gulf from $22.60 a week earlier.
